label: bug
file: src/notifications/rollup.ts

The rollup is scheduled by a single hourly tick (`startRollupSchedule`) that fires at the top of each UTC hour and then calls `isRollupDue`, which compares `localHour(now, user.timezone)` to `SEND_HOUR` and checks that `now` falls within the first day of the user's local week (`weekStart`).

For users whose UTC offset is ahead of UTC (e.g. Sydney, UTC+10/+11), the local-week boundary computed from `now` can land on the wrong side of the server's hourly tick grid compared to users behind or at UTC (e.g. London), so the "within the first day of week" window check silently misses the correct tick and only catches it on a later (Tuesday local) tick. That's why London users, who are closer to/behind UTC, get the email right on Monday while Sydney users get it a tick late, on Tuesday morning local time.

The scheduling/window logic in `sendWeeklyRollups`/`isRollupDue` needs to correctly account for positive UTC offsets so the due-check reliably matches the hourly tick for all time zones, not just those at or behind UTC.
